paras.en: That was how I learnt a second very important thing: the planet he came from was barely bigger than a house!
paras.zh: 我就这样知道了第二件很重要的事：他原来住的星球，只比一座房子大一点点！

paras.en: That could not surprise me very much. I knew very well that besides the large planets like Earth, Jupiter, Mars and Venus, which have been given names, there are hundreds of others, sometimes so small that they are very hard to see through a telescope. When an astronomer discovers one of them, he gives it a number for a name. He calls it, for example, “asteroid 3251.”
paras.zh: 这倒不会让我太惊讶。我很清楚，除了地球、木星、火星、金星这些有名字的大行星，还有几百颗别的星球，有些小得连用望远镜都很难看见。天文学家发现其中一颗时，就给它一个编号当名字。比如，他会叫它“3251号小行星”。

paras.en: I have good reasons to believe that the planet the little prince came from is asteroid B 612.
paras.zh: 我有充分的理由相信，小王子来自的星球，就是小行星B 612。

paras.en: This asteroid has been seen through a telescope only once, in 1909, by a Turkish astronomer.
paras.zh: 这颗小行星只被人用望远镜看到过一次，那是在1909年，看到它的是一位土耳其天文学家。

paras.en: He had then given a grand presentation of his discovery at an International Congress of Astronomy.
paras.zh: 当时，他在一次国际天文学大会上，对自己的发现作了一番隆重的论证。

paras.en: But no one had believed him because of his clothes. Grown-ups are like that.
paras.zh: 可就因为他的穿着，没有人相信他。大人们就是这样。

paras.en: Luckily for the reputation of asteroid B 612, a Turkish dictator ordered his people to wear European clothes or face death. The astronomer gave his presentation again in 1920, wearing a very elegant suit. And this time everyone agreed with him.
paras.zh: 对小行星B 612的名声来说，幸运的是，一位土耳其独裁者命令他的国民穿欧洲式的衣服，违者处以死刑。1920年，那位天文学家穿着一身十分雅致的衣服，再次作了论证。这一回，所有人都赞同他了。

paras.en: If I have told you these details about asteroid B 612, and if I have shared its number with you, it is because of grown-ups. Grown-ups love numbers. When you tell them about a new friend, they never ask about the things that matter. They never say, “What does his voice sound like? Which games does he like best? Does he collect butterflies?” They ask, “How old is he? How many brothers does he have? How much does he weigh? How much does his father earn?” Only then do they think they know him. If you tell grown-ups, “I saw a beautiful house made of pink bricks, with geraniums at the windows and doves on the roof…” they cannot picture that house. You have to tell them, “I saw a house worth a hundred thousand francs.” Then they cry out, “How pretty!”
paras.zh: 我之所以告诉你们这些关于小行星B 612的细节，之所以把它的编号也告诉你们，都是因为大人们。大人们喜欢数字。当你向他们说起一个新朋友时，他们从来不问要紧的事。他们从来不说：“他的声音是什么样的？他最喜欢玩什么游戏？他收集蝴蝶吗？”他们问的是：“他几岁了？他有几个兄弟？他有多重？他爸爸挣多少钱？”只有这样，他们才觉得自己了解他了。如果你对大人们说：“我看见了一座美丽的房子，用粉红色的砖砌成，窗边有天竺葵，屋顶上有鸽子……”他们就想象不出那座房子的样子。你得对他们说：“我看见了一座值十万法郎的房子。”这时他们就会喊道：“多漂亮啊！”

paras.en: So if you tell them, “The proof that the little prince existed is that he was delightful, that he laughed, and that he wanted a sheep. When you want a sheep, that is proof that you exist,” they will shrug their shoulders and call you a child! But if you tell them, “The planet he came from is asteroid B 612,” then they will be convinced, and they will stop bothering you with their questions. That is how they are. You must not hold it against them. Children must be very forgiving towards grown-ups.
paras.zh: 所以，如果你对他们说：“小王子存在过的证据，就是他那么可爱，他笑过，他想要一只绵羊。一个人想要一只绵羊，就证明他存在。”他们就会耸耸肩，说你是个孩子！可如果你对他们说：“他来的那颗星球是小行星B 612。”他们就会信服，不再拿问题来烦你。他们就是这样。不要怪他们。孩子们得对大人们十分宽容。

paras.en: But of course, we who understand life do not care about numbers at all! I would have liked to begin this story the way fairy tales begin. I would have liked to say:
paras.zh: 不过，当然了，我们这些懂得生活的人，才不在乎那些编号呢！我本想像讲童话那样，开始讲这个故事。我本想这样说：

paras.en: “Once upon a time, there was a little prince who lived on a planet barely bigger than himself, and who needed a friend...” To those who understand life, that would have seemed much truer.
paras.zh: “从前，有一个小王子，住在一颗只比他大一点点的星球上，他需要一个朋友……”对那些懂得生活的人来说，这样听起来会真实得多。

paras.en: For I do not like people to read my book lightly. It brings me so much sorrow to tell of these memories. It has already been six years since my friend went away with his sheep. If I try to describe him here, it is so that I will not forget him. It is sad to forget a friend. Not everyone has had a friend. And I could become like grown-ups who are no longer interested in anything but numbers. That is another reason why I bought a box of paints and some pencils. It is hard to take up drawing again at my age, when your only attempts were a closed boa constrictor and an open boa constrictor, at the age of six! Of course, I will try to make the portraits look as much like him as possible. But I am not quite sure I will succeed. One drawing looks right, and the next no longer looks like him. I get his height a little wrong too. Here the little prince is too tall. There he is too short. I am unsure about the colour of his suit too. So I feel my way, trying this and that, as best I can. I will also get some more important details wrong. But you will have to forgive me for that. My friend never gave explanations. Perhaps he thought I was like him. But I, unfortunately, do not know how to see sheep through crates. Perhaps I am a little like grown-ups. I must have grown older.
paras.zh: 因为我不喜欢别人随随便便地读我的书。讲起这些往事，我心里有那么多悲伤。我的朋友带着他的绵羊离开，已经六年了。我在这里试着描绘他，是为了不把他忘掉。忘掉一个朋友，是件难过的事。并不是每个人都曾有过一个朋友。而我也可能变得像那些除了数字，已经不再对别的事物感兴趣的大人们一样。所以，这也是我买了一盒颜料和几支铅笔的原因。到了我这个年纪，从前又只在六岁时试着画过一条合着的蟒蛇和一条剖开的蟒蛇，要重新拿起画笔，真不容易！当然，我会尽量把他的画像画得像他。但我并没有十足的把握能画好。这一幅还行，另一幅又不像了。他的个子，我也画得有些不准。这一幅里的小王子太高了。那一幅里的他又太矮了。他那身衣服的颜色，我也拿不定主意。于是我这样试试，那样试试，勉勉强强地摸索着。还有一些更重要的细节，我也会弄错。不过，这些就得请你们原谅我了。我的朋友从来不作解释。他也许以为我和他一样。可惜，我却不懂得怎样透过箱子看见里面的绵羊。我也许有点像大人们了。我一定是变老了。
